definitions.explanation: A medication that induces calm or sleep by reducing nervous system activity.

examples.japanese: {医者|いしゃ}が{鎮静剤|ちんせいざい}を{投与|とうよ}した。
{手術|しゅじゅつ}{前|まえ}に{鎮静剤|ちんせいざい}を{打|う}たれて{眠|ねむ}くなった。
examples.english: I became sleepy after being given a sedative before surgery.

examples.japanese: {興奮|こうふん}した{患者|かんじゃ}を{落|お}ち{着|つ}かせるために{鎮静剤|ちんせいざい}が{使|つか}われることがある。
examples.english: Sedatives are sometimes used to calm an agitated patient.

notes:
Composed of {鎮静|ちんせい} (calming, sedation) + {剤|ざい} (agent, medicine). Used in medical contexts for medications that reduce anxiety, induce sleep, or calm agitated patients. Not to be confused with pain medication or anesthesia, which have different purposes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鎮静剤|ちんせいざい}を{投与|とうよ}する — administer a sedative
- {鎮静剤|ちんせいざい}を{打|う}つ — give a sedative injection
- {鎮静剤|ちんせいざい}の{効果|こうか} — effect of the sedative
- {鎮静剤|ちんせいざい}が{効|き}く — the sedative takes effect

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {鎮痛剤|ちんつうざい} — painkiller, analgesic; reduces pain rather than inducing calm
- {睡眠薬|すいみんやく} — sleeping pill; specifically induces sleep, while {鎮静剤|ちんせいざい} primarily calms
- {麻酔|ますい} — anesthesia; eliminates sensation entirely, used for surgical procedures
